newsitem.title: UK: Kleinwort hikes Q4 oil price forecast by $3.50.
newsitem.headline: Kleinwort hikes Q4 oil price forecast by $3.50.

text.p: Strong global oil demand, low heating fuel inventories and rising political concerns about supply have led brokers Kleinwort Benson to raise by a substantial $3.50 a barrel its fourth quarter oil price forecast.

In its global world oil market report, Kleinwort said it now expects North Sea crude oil Brent, which serves as a world benchmark, to average $23 a barrel in the final three months of the year for an annual average of $20.40.
But oil prices are more likely to fall in early 1997 than rise, it said.
Kleinwort said winter oil trading is likely to be volatile but that most bullish news has already been factored into current prices.
"Oil prices may go even higher short-term but the market has for months been fed bullish news which must by now have largely been discounted," it said.

Oil prices earlier this week hit post-Gulf War highs mostly on the back of strong heating oil buying ahead of the winter. Stocks of distillates, mostly heating fuel, on both sides of the Atlantic are much lower than last year.
Brent is hovering around $23.75, nearly $8 over last year's levels.
But signs of some stock rebuilding resulted in a midweek selloff though traders said there is a reluctance to sell the market short as the peak winter demand period has yet to hit.
However, the London-based brokerage said winter demand "may disappoint" especially if last year's frigid temperatures are not repeated.

"Sustained high heating oil prices could induce conservation and substitution (in favour of natural gas), especially in the U.S.," Kleinwort said. Kleinwort also expects oil production outside the Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries to rise by nearly two million barrels per day (bpd) year on year in the first quarter 1997.
This rise is well above Kleinwort's original 1997 forecast and is mostly due to new production from oil field projects that had been postponed this year.
